raw_segments.text: As to the manner in which the ignorance is removed and the man of imperfect self-control
recovers his knowledge, the account is the same as with respect to him who is drunk or
asleep and is not peculiar to this affection, so physiologists are the right people to apply
But whereas the minor premise of every practical syllogism is an opinion on matter cognizable
by sense and determines the actions, he who is under the influence of passion either has
not this, or so has it that his having does not amount to knowing, but merely saying,
as a man when drunk might repeat Empedocles verses.
And because the minor term is neither universal, nor is thought to have the power of producing
knowledge in like manner as the universal term.
And so the result which Socrates was seeking comes out, that is to say, the affection does
not take place in the presence of that which is thought to be specially and properly knowledge,
nor is this dragged about by reason of the affection, but in the presence of that knowledge
